purpose: Focused Brazilian hard-case regression slice for adjacent model-year contradictions and cross-source identity observations with materially incomplete model-year or transmission/powertrain evidence. Expected outcomes are curated product decisions grounded in official sources, not resolver-generated labels.

cases.rationale: Independent official Volkswagen launch and technical material establish the same Highline 250 TSI automatic configuration; the absence of model-year evidence on both observations is not itself a contradiction.

Toyota documents the same named Brazilian Corolla trim in model years 2025 and 2026; under the selected Senatran-aligned catalog policy, explicit adjacent model-year non-overlap is a deterministic identity contradiction.
Chevrolet documents Premier in adjacent Onix model years 2026 and 2027; the shared trim name does not override explicit model-year non-overlap.

The detailed price list identifies the Premier mechanical configuration, while the engineering article establishes a 2026 Premier hatch but does not map that trim to a specific powertrain/transmission. The incomplete observation must not be auto-collapsed into the detailed one.

The current product page lists Highline 250 TSI and transmission choices only at range level. Because transmission is identity-defining and version-specific mapping is absent from that observation, the pair remains REVIEW rather than inheriting the older six-speed mapping silently.

One official observation has complete Highline 250 TSI mechanical identity but no model year, while the MY26 evidence set establishes the same 250 TSI/six-speed T-Cross mechanical family in model-year context. The selected policy requires REVIEW when model-year evidence is present on only one side absent stronger identity proof.
